title: Concurrency collapse rehearsal — scratch notes
content:
Objective:
Run a controlled ‘rehearsal’ that intentionally pushes the serving stack to a concurrency collapse point and observe graceful degradation / recovery behavior. Goal is to (1) identify the early indicators of collapse, (2) validate fallback routing and throttling behaviors, and (3) produce an actionable checklist for on-call and autoscaling tuning.

Notes on why this is different:
- Not a pure steady-state QPS sweep. Instead we create a lockstep ramp + short microbursts to trigger KV cache churn + hot GPU scheduling contention.
- Emphasis on transition metrics (the first 30s of a collapse) rather than long-run averages.

Environment:
- Serving runtime: local replica from feature/backpressure-tuning branch (git rev: 7a3d9f4)
- Model: gpt-ish 13B FP16 (quantized variant used for some runs) — image placeholder name: redwood/13b-serve-q4f16
- Hardware: A10G single-GPU instance (4 vCPU coach for proxy), 64GB RAM
- Config: max_concurrency_per_gpu = 48; continuous_batching enabled; default batch timeout = 8ms; KV cache capacity ~ 6M tokens; prefetch disabled.
- Traffic generator: fortio for steady phases + custom script (rehearsal-driver.py) to emit lockstep bursts.

Experiment plan (high level):
1) Warm baseline: steady 250 QPS, observe metrics for 3m (cache warm).
2) Lockstep ramp: every 30s increase QPS by 50 until 800 QPS, while also injecting a 3s microburst at double current QPS every 45s to cause short-lived queueing.
3) Collapse trigger: at 800 QPS introduce a ~12s simultaneous fanout spike (sends 600 concurrent requests almost instantly) — this is the rehearsed failure mode.
4) Recovery: enable (a) soft backpressure (reject fraction policy), (b) fallback routing to quantized model variant, (c) scaledown/tokenshed experiments in different runs.
5) Repeat with cold cache (restart runtime) and compare.

Commands used (rough):
- fortio load -c 16 -qps 250 -t 180s http://proxy:8080/api/generate
- python rehearsal-driver.py --ramp 50 --step 30 --burst 3s --max 800 --fanout 600
- collect metrics via /metrics and tailor PromQL snapshots (scraped every 5s)

Key metrics captured (sample slices):
- request.qps (ingress)
- serving.tokens_per_sec (tokens/s processed)
- queue.length (per-proxy queue)
- p50, p95, p99 latency (ms) end-to-end
- gpu_utilization (%) and gpu_mem_used (GB)
- kvcache.eviction_rate and kvcache.hit_rate

Representative numbers (Warm baseline @250 QPS — avg over 3m):
- QPS: 250
- p50: 48 ms
- p95: 123 ms
- p99: 290 ms
- gpu_util: 62%
- kvcache.hit_rate: 0.88

During lockstep ramp (at 500 QPS sustained):
- QPS: 500
- p50: 82 ms
- p95: 210 ms
- p99: 520 ms
- observed queue length spikes to 160 requests for ~2–4s during microbursts
- kvcache.eviction bursts observed when fanout hits; hit_rate drops to 0.65 briefly

Collapse trigger run (fanout 600 concurrent sends):
- immediate effects: proxy queue jumps > 1000 entries in <1s, request latencies hit manual timeouts (60s) for ~8–12s window
- p50 for surviving requests: 320 ms; p95: 2.3s; p99: >10s (many timed out)
- GPU utilization: saturated at 98–100% with frequent context-switching and small kernel stalls
- KV cache: massive eviction ramp — eviction_rate x10 baseline, hit_rate drops to ~0.12
- Observed server-side OOM warnings for prefetch buffers in 2 trials (need to inspect mem accounting)

Recovery runs (three approaches tested):
A) Soft backpressure = immediate fractional reject (throttle) when queue length > 200
- result: reduced timed-out requests by ~75%; throughput falls to ~320 QPS but p99 improves from >10s down to 1.4s
- side effect: user-visible 429s spike, but fewer stuck tails.

B) Fallback routing to quantized variant (auto-fallback policy triggers when latency > 1s sustained for 5s)
- result: after fallback engaged, effective tokens/s rises (quantized faster); p99 drops to ~650 ms; perceived quality regress slightly (temp test prompts show occasional tokenization artifacts)
- transition jitter: 2–4s while ongoing requests drain and new requests hit fallback path.

C) Aggressive scaling (spin up reserve instance / preemptive warm pool)
- result: scale-up reduces queue to <100 within 10s, p95/p99 back near ramp phase values. Costly and not instant on this infra; prewarmed pool looked necessary.

Quick ASCII table summary (selected snapshots):
Phase           | QPS  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | kv_hit | gpu_util
Warm            | 250  | 48      | 123     | 290     | 0.88   | 62%
Ramp (500)      | 500  | 82      | 210     | 520     | 0.65   | 85%
Collapse spike  | ~800 | 320     | 2300    | >10000  | 0.12   | 99%
Soft backpress  | 320  | 140     | 400     | 1400    | 0.4    | 92%
Fallback quant   | 420  | 95      | 220     | 650     | 0.55   | 88%

Top observations / heuristics:
- The first reliable early-warning signal is kvcache.eviction_rate rising consistently for 6+ seconds; queue length often lags behind that. Consider alerting on eviction_rate > 3x baseline for 10s window.
- GPU saturation + kernel stalls coincide with long p99 tails; this is different from long queuing-only tails where gpu_util sits <90%.
- Fractional/rejection backpressure recovers fastest but trades off UX (429s). Good candidate as an emergency policy.
- Fallback to quantized model gives best middle-ground for reducing tails without user-visible 4xxs, but needs warm pool of quantized instances to be less jittery.
- Prewarming reserve instances is effective but needs cost/benefit analysis (we saw 10s cold spin-up vs 2–3s warm handoff).
- Tune batch timeout upward (8ms -> 12–15ms) to reduce kernel churn during microbursts; we observed better packing at cost of ~5–10ms baseline increase.

Actionable next steps:
- Add a short-lived alert rule: kvcache.eviction_rate > 3x baseline for 15s OR gpu_kernel_stall_rate > threshold -> trigger on-call page + automated throttle script.
- Implement fractional reject policy with ramped backoff (start 10% -> 50% over 8s) as a trial on staging.
- Prototype prewarmed quantized pool and add quick-fallback orchestration (target cold start <3s).
- Re-run rehearsal with network jitter enabled and different model sizes (7B/30B) to map sensitivity.
- Investigate memory accounting for prefetch buffers (two OOM traces).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Does eviction_rate threshold generalize across model sizes and multi-tenant noisy neighbors? Run cross-tenant rehearsal.
- UX surface: how to return helpful 429 body that indicates expected retry window? (work with DX).
- Validate quality regression quantitatively for quantized fallback (A/B prompts and BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or human evals).

Personal notes:
- This felt close to a production incident profile — good rehearsal. Felt the backpressure policy implemented in the feature branch is promising but needs a safety net (fallback + prewarm).
- Keep the rehearsal-driver script; can be reused as on-call test harness.

Attachments / logs: 
- Prom screenshots: /tmp/prom_snapshots/2024-11-20-rehearsal/*
- raw traces: s3://redwood-inference-test-logs/rehearsal/2024-11-20/ (permissioned)
- rehearsal-driver.py in repo: tools/loadtests/rehearsal-driver.py

Notes-to-self: turn this into a short runbook after action items validated. Will sync with Samir and SRE next week (tentative: Mon 11/25).
